payload.goal:
Add order priority and backorders to this warehouse codebase, across every layer that already exists.

Domain  - src/domain/orders.ts:
- Export type OrderPriority = "standard" | "express".
- Order gains a readonly priority field of that type. It is optional at the call site: an order placed without a priority is treated as "standard", so existing callers keep working unchanged.
- placeOrder throws OrderError when a priority is supplied and is neither "standard" nor "express".
- Export interface Backorder with readonly orderId, skuId and missing fields, where missing is a positive integer.
- WarehouseState gains a readonly backorders field keyed by order id.
- reserveOrder records a Backorder for every line whose quantity exceeds the available units, instead of throwing, and leaves the order in a status from which it can still be cancelled.
- Export listBackorders(state) returning every recorded Backorder.

Application  - src/application/warehouse-service.ts:
- The service exposes the new operations and emits a warehouse event for a recorded backorder.

Fulfillment  - src/fulfillment/planner.ts:
- Within one wave, planFulfillment lists express orders before standard ones. Its existing signature does not change.

Durability  - src/durability/journal.ts:
- HistoryAnalytics gains a backorders count derived from the events.

API  - src/api/server.ts:
- The server exposes the backorders of the current state.

Presentation  - src/presentation/tower.ts:
- The rendered SVG distinguishes express orders from standard ones.

Probe  - src/probe/g6.ts and a package script named study:g6-probe:
- Follow the shape of the existing probes: export main() returning a JSON string, and write exactly one JSON object to stdout when invoked directly, with no other output.
- Two invocations from the same commit must emit byte-identical output.

Preserve all existing behaviour and keep every existing test passing. Put new tests next to the code they cover, inside the directories the test script already scans.

scripts.test: node --test src/domain/*.test.ts src/probe/*.test.ts src/scenarios/*.test.ts src/application/*.test.ts src/presentation/*.test.ts src/api/*.test.ts src/fulfillment/*.test.ts src/durability/*.test.ts

root.title: Order priority and backorders rollout
root.objective: Add optional order priority and backorder handling across the warehouse stack without breaking existing behavior.
expectedOutcomes: Orders default to standard priority, validate supplied priorities, and record backorders in warehouse state.
The service, API, journal, planner, and presentation layers all consume the shared contract consistently.
A new study:g6-probe script emits byte-identical one-object JSON output from a main() entrypoint.
New regression tests live beside the touched code and the existing suite remains green.

complexitySignals.rationale: The change crosses every existing layer, adds new domain state and validation, and needs deterministic probe behavior plus regression coverage.

cut.rationale: The feature spans multiple already-existing boundaries, but each layer can be verified independently if the shared order/backorder contract is split by consumer-facing seams.

children.title: Domain order model and backorder state
children.objective: Extend order state and reservation logic to accept optional priority, preserve standard defaulting, and record backorders instead of throwing on partial shortfall.
expectedOutcomes: OrderPriority is exported as standard or express, and omitted priority still behaves as standard.
placeOrder rejects invalid supplied priorities with OrderError.
WarehouseState carries backorders keyed by order id, reserveOrder records them, and listBackorders returns them.

children.title: Warehouse service backorder propagation
children.objective: Surface backorder-aware warehouse operations through the service and emit a warehouse event when a backorder is recorded.
expectedOutcomes: The service exposes the new backorder-aware operations expected by callers.
A recorded backorder produces a warehouse event with the necessary identifiers and missing quantity.
Existing service behavior remains intact for non-backorder flows.

children.title: Wave planner priority ordering
children.objective: Keep the existing planner signature and order express orders ahead of standard orders within each wave.
expectedOutcomes: Within one wave, express orders are planned before standard orders.
The existing planner signature and other wave behavior do not change.
Regression tests capture the relative ordering rule.

children.title: Journal backorder analytics
children.objective: Derive a backorders count in HistoryAnalytics from the journal event stream.
expectedOutcomes: HistoryAnalytics includes a backorders count derived from events.
The count reflects the journaled backorder records and does not depend on unrelated state.
Regression tests cover the new analytics field.

children.title: API backorder exposure
children.objective: Expose current-state backorders from the server response without changing the rest of the API shape.
expectedOutcomes: The server response includes the current state's backorders.
The rest of the API contract remains unchanged.
API tests assert the new field is present and correctly shaped.

children.title: Tower SVG priority rendering
children.objective: Render express orders distinctly from standard orders in the tower SVG output.
expectedOutcomes: The rendered SVG visually distinguishes express orders from standard orders.
The distinction is stable enough for existing presentation tests to assert.
No unrelated visual behavior changes.

children.title: G6 probe script and deterministic output
children.objective: Add a study:g6-probe entry and src/probe/g6.ts so main() returns a JSON string and direct execution writes exactly one JSON object deterministically.
expectedOutcomes: package.json exposes a study:g6-probe script that runs the new probe entrypoint.
src/probe/g6.ts exports main() returning a JSON string.
Direct execution prints exactly one JSON object to stdout and repeated runs from the same commit are byte-identical.
Probe tests live in src/probe and are discovered by the existing test script.

repositoryEvidence.observation: The domain orders module exists and is the natural place for priority normalization, backorder records, and reservation semantics.
Co-located domain tests already exist, so the new priority and backorder behavior can be regression-tested beside the model.
The application service is already the orchestration boundary for warehouse behavior and can emit a backorder event from there.
Service-level tests already exist, which makes it straightforward to lock in the new service-facing operations and event emission.
The fulfillment planner exists as the wave-ordering boundary where express-before-standard logic belongs.
Planner tests already exist, so the within-wave ordering change can be verified without introducing a new harness.
The journal layer already owns history analytics, making it the right place to derive the backorders count from events.
Journal tests are present, so analytics changes can be covered where the derivation is implemented.
The API server already exposes warehouse state and can surface the current state's backorders alongside existing fields.
API tests already exist and can pin the response shape when backorders are exposed.
The tower renderer exists as the SVG presentation boundary where express versus standard order styling can be distinguished.
Presentation tests already exist, giving a direct place to verify the visual distinction encoded in the SVG output.
The repo already has a probe pattern with a direct main() entrypoint, which the new g6 probe should match.
Probe behavior is already tested next to the probe code, so the new g6 probe can follow the same adjacency convention.
The package manifest already owns scripts and test discovery, so adding study:g6-probe belongs in the same executable scope as the existing study and test scripts.
The existing probe script already runs a source file directly with node, which is the shape the new g6 probe should follow.
The test script already scans src/probe/*.test.ts, so a new g6 probe test can be placed in the existing discovery path.
